_meta.indication: Treatment of the signs and symptoms of early-stage idiopathic Parkinson's disease

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, dose-response, multicenter, multinational study with fixed doses (2, 4, 6, or 8 mg/24 hours) vs placebo for up to 11 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Early-stage idiopathic Parkinson's disease patients not receiving concomitant dopamine agonist therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in combined UPDRS Part II (activities of daily living) plus Part III (motor) scores
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in UPDRS (II+III): -3.5, -4.5, -6.3, -6.3 for 2, 4, 6, 8 mg/24 hours respectively vs -1.4 for placebo; differences from placebo -2.1, -3.1, -4.9, -5.0; statistically significant improvement at the three highest doses

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multinational, flexible-dose (up to 6 mg/24 hours), parallel-group study in North America, Neupro vs placebo (2:1), up to ~28 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Early-stage idiopathic Parkinson's disease patients in North America
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in combined UPDRS Part II plus Part III scores
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in UPDRS (II+III): -4.0 for Neupro vs +1.39 for placebo, a difference from placebo of -5.3, statistically significant

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multinational, flexible-dose (up to 8 mg/24 hours), three-arm, parallel-group, double-dummy study of placebo vs Neupro vs active oral comparator (1:2:2) up to ~39 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Early-stage Parkinson's disease patients at sites outside North America
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in combined UPDRS Part II plus Part III scores
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in UPDRS (II+III): -6.83 for Neupro vs -2.33 for placebo, a difference from placebo of -4.5, statistically significant

key_safety: Most common adverse events (Neupro N=649 vs placebo N=289): nausea 38% vs 15%, application site reactions 37% vs 14%, dizziness 18% vs 11%, headache 14% vs 10%, vomiting 13% vs 2%; somnolence and falling asleep during activities of daily living are notable risks
target_moa: Rotigotine is a non-ergoline D3/D2/D1 dopamine agonist; its effect in Parkinson's disease is thought to be related to stimulation of dopamine D2 receptors within the caudate-putamen in the brain

description.text: Added indication to treat the signs and symptoms of moderate to severe primary Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS)

citations.quote: The "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug application S-001 proposes an added indication to treat "the signs and symptoms of moderate to severe primary Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS)" and supplemental application S-002 proposes an added indication to treat "the signs and symptoms of advanced Parkinson's disease (APD)."

description.text: Added indication for moderate-to-severe primary Restless Legs Syndrome

citations.quote: Neupro (Rotigotine Transdermal System) is indicated for the treatment of moderate-to-severe primary restless legs syndrome.

basis.text: The application carried a Standard priority designation

summary.text: NDA 21-829 for rotigotine transdermal system for early-stage Parkinson's disease was received January 28, 2005 under 505(b) with a Standard review designation; FDA issued an approvable letter on February 28, 2006 requesting additional analyses, and the application was approved following the sponsor's complete response, with postmarketing study commitments

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated January 19, 2005, received January 28, 2005, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
On 2/28/06, an approvable letter was issued with requests for several additional analyses.
We remind you of your postmarketing study commitments in your submission dated May 4, 2007. These commitments are listed below.

requirement.text: Complete the thorough QTc study characterizing the effects of rotigotine on cardiac repolarization in humans and submit the final study report

citations.quote: To complete your thorough QTc study characterizing the effects of rotigotine on cardiac repolarization in humans and submit the final study report.

requirement.text: Complete the echocardiographic study in Parkinson's disease patients comparing effects of different dopamine agonists, including rotigotine, on echocardiographic measures to determine if rotigotine is associated with cardiac valvulopathy

citations.quote: To complete the echocardiographic study in patients with Parkinson's disease comparing the effects of different dopamine agonists, including rotigotine, on echocardiographic measures. This study will help determine if rotigotine is associated with the cardiac valvulopathy seen with some other dopamine agonists.

requirement.text: Complete a fixed-dose dose-response study of rotigotine in advanced Parkinson's disease incorporating monitoring of laboratory parameters related to hematopoiesis and renal function, including post-treatment washout to assess reversibility

citations.quote: To complete a fixed-dose dose-response study of rotigotine in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease that incorporates monitoring of laboratory parameters related primarily to hematopoiesis and renal function
